cards.title: Pharaoh Commanding Haman to Build a Tower to the Ropes of the Heavens
cards.note: In Surah 40:36–37, Pharaoh orders Haman to build a tower (sarhan) to reach the 'ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat) and look upon Moses' God, merging Genesis 11:3–4 (Babel), Esther 3:1 (Haman), and the aerial castle of the Story of Ahikar.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Pharaoh commanded his vizier Haman to construct a high brick tower in Egypt so Pharaoh could ascend toward the pathways of the sky and test Moses' claim regarding the God of heaven.
discussion.reply: Unlike 28:38, which specifies baking clay bricks, 40:36–37 focuses on reaching the 'ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat). The passage merges three ancient traditions separated by centuries: the Tower of Babel built to reach heaven in Genesis 11:3–4, the Persian court minister Haman under King Artaxerxes in Esther 3:1, and Pharaoh's demand for a castle between heaven and earth in the Story of Ahikar.

cards.quranEn: [36] Pharaoh said, ‘Haman! Build a tower for me, so that I may reach the ropes, [37] the ropes of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses. Surely I think he is a liar indeed.’ In this way the evil of his deed was made to appear enticing to Pharaoh, and he was kept from the way. But the plot of Pharaoh only (came) to ruin.
quranHighlights: Pharaoh said, ‘Haman! Build a tower for me, so that I may reach the ropes,
the ropes of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses.

sources.title: Genesis
sources.en: And a man said to his neighbor, Come, let us make bricks and bake them with fire. And the brick was to them for stone, and their mortar was bitumen. And they said, Come, let us build to ourselves a city and tower, whose top shall be to heaven, and let us make to ourselves a name, before we are scattered abroad upon the face of all the earth.
highlights: Come, let us build to ourselves a city and tower, whose top shall be to heaven

sources.title: Esther
sources.en: And after this king Artaxerxes highly honored Aman [son] of Amadathes, the Bugaean, and exalted him, and set his seat above all his friends.
highlights: king Artaxerxes highly honored Aman [son] of Amadathes, the Bugaean, and exalted him

sources.title: The Story of Ahikar (Aramaic/Syriac Recension — Pharaoh's Aerial Castle)
sources.ref: Story of Ahikar 5:2 (tr. J. Rendel Harris / F. C. Conybeare)
sources.workSub: The Story of Ahikar (Aramaic/Syriac Recension — Pharaoh's Aerial Castle)
sources.en: I have been desiring to build a castle between the heaven and the earth, and I want thee to send me a wise, clever man from thyself to build it for me, and to answer me all my questions, and that I may have the taxes and the custom duties of Assyria for three years.’
highlights: I have been desiring to build a castle between the heaven and the earth

cards.quranAr: وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ ٱبۡنِ لِي صَرۡحٗا لَّعَلِّيٓ أَبۡلُغُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَٰبَ ﴿36﴾ أَسۡبَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُۥ كَٰذِبٗاۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرۡعَوۡنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِۚ وَمَا كَيۡدُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِلَّا فِي تَبَابٖ ﴿37﴾
